problem: Given that $a=⟨-2,4,3⟩,$ $b=⟨-1,3,2⟩,$ and $c=⟨2,-1,4⟩,$ find $a\cdot (b\times c)$ using the definition of the scalar triple product.
worked_solution:
First, we find the cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}b\times c & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(3\cdot 4-2\cdot (-1))i-((-1)\cdot 4-2\cdot 2)j+((-1)\cdot (-1)-3\cdot 2)k \\  & =14i+8j-5k \\  & =⟨14,8,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the scalar triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨-2,4,3⟩\cdot ⟨14,8,-5⟩ \\  & =(-2)\cdot 14+4\cdot 8+3\cdot (-5) \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$
